title.rendered: He Gave Thanks and Broke the Bread: Thanks Over Too Little | The Thankful Heart, Day 5

excerpt.rendered: Matthew 14:19-20: Jesus gave thanks over five loaves and two fish, and all were filled. Day 5 of The Thankful Heart thanks God over too little.

content.rendered:
Five loaves and two fish for a crowd of thousands. It was nowhere near enough. Jesus looked up to heaven and gave thanks for it anyway, and what was too little in human hands became more than enough in His.

The Gospel For Today | Thursday, November 19, 2026 | The Thankful Heart, Day 5

Today’s Scripture

“Then He commanded the multitudes to sit down on the grass. And He took the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up to heaven, He blessed and broke and gave the loaves to the disciples; and the disciples gave to the multitudes. So they all ate and were filled, and they took up twelve baskets full of the fragments that remained.”
Matthew 14:19-20 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

The disciples had done the maths, and the maths was bad. A huge crowd, a remote place, the day wearing on, and nothing to feed anyone. Their solution was sensible: send the people away to buy food in the villages. Jesus answered with words that must have sounded impossible: “You give them something to eat.” All they could find was a boy’s lunch. “We have here only five loaves and two fish.”

Listen to that word “only.” It is the word we use when what we have looks small next to what we face. Only one salary for the whole family. Only a little strength left. Only a few people in the church plant in Sao Paulo. Only a small idea and no funding. We hold up our five loaves and two fish and feel embarrassed by them.

Jesus said, “Bring them here to Me.” Then He did something remarkable. Before a single loaf multiplied, looking up to heaven, He blessed. In John’s account of the same miracle, we are told plainly that He gave thanks (John 6:11). He did not complain about the size of the supply. He did not wait for it to grow before He was grateful. He gave thanks over too little, and then He broke it and handed it out.

The result? “They all ate and were filled.” Not a nibble each. Filled. And twelve baskets of leftovers, one for every doubting disciple to carry. Thanksgiving did not shrink the problem. It placed the small supply into the hands of the One for whom nothing is too little. Paul would later write that God is able to make all grace abound toward you, that you, always having all sufficiency in all things, may have an abundance for every good work (2 Corinthians 9:8).

So what is in your hands today that feels like only five loaves? Do not hide it. Bring it to Him. Lift your eyes and thank the Father for it, as it is, before it changes. Then break it and give it away. The miracle of multiplication still happens in the hands of a thankful heart.

How the Thankful Heart Sees Supply

It brings the little to Jesus. “Bring them here to Me” is still His word over what feels too small.

It gives thanks before the increase. Jesus blessed the loaves while they were still only five.

It expects more than enough. They all ate, were filled, and twelve baskets remained.

Declaration

Lord, I thank You for what is already in my hands. I bring it to You and I give thanks over it, just as Jesus did with the loaves and the fish (Matthew 14:19). I thank You that You are able to make all grace abound toward me, so that, always having all sufficiency in all things, I have an abundance for every good work (2 Corinthians 9:8). I thank You that my God has supplied all my need according to His riches in glory by Christ Jesus (Philippians 4:19). What feels like too little is more than enough in Your hands. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
